explanationUz: Past Simple — o‘tgan zamonda boshlanib, tugagan ish-harakat uchun ishlatiladi: “Kecha futbol o‘ynadim” = I played football yesterday. Odatda gapda vaqt ko‘rsatkichi bo‘ladi: yesterday, last week, last Saturday, two days ago, in 2020.

To‘g‘ri (regular) fe’llarga -ed qo‘shiladi va shakl hamma shaxsda bir xil: I played, she played, they played. Imlo qoidalari: e bilan tugasa faqat -d (live → lived); undosh + y bo‘lsa y → i (study → studied); qisqa unli + bitta undosh bo‘lsa undosh ikkilanadi (stop → stopped).

Inkor va so‘roqda yordamchi fe’l did ishlatiladi, asosiy fe’l esa BOSHLANG‘ICH shaklga qaytadi: I did not (didn’t) visit my aunt. Did you visit your aunt? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn’t. “Did you visited” deb aytilmaydi — -ed faqat tasdiq gapda.

“Ago” vaqtdan KEYIN keladi: three days ago (uch kun oldin), a week ago. “Last” esa oldin: last Monday, last summer. O‘zbekchadagi “o‘tgan shanba” = last Saturday, “o‘tgan shanbada” deb “in last Saturday” yozilmaydi — old qo‘shimcha kerak emas.

grammar.titleUz: Past Simple: noto‘g‘ri fe’llar va was / were
grammar.titleEn: Past Simple: irregular verbs and was / were
explanationUz: Ko‘p ishlatiladigan fe’llarning o‘tgan zamon shakli -ed bilan emas, alohida yasaladi — ular noto‘g‘ri (irregular) fe’llar: go → went, see → saw, have → had, eat → ate, make → made, come → came, take → took, give → gave, get → got. Bu shakllarni yod olish kerak, qoida yo‘q.

Noto‘g‘ri fe’llarda ham inkor va so‘roq did bilan yasaladi va fe’l boshlang‘ich shaklga qaytadi: I went → I didn’t go → Did you go? “Did you went” deb aytilmaydi. Shu sababli inkor va so‘roqda to‘g‘ri-noto‘g‘ri fe’l farqi yo‘qoladi.

To be fe’lining o‘tgan zamoni ikki shaklga ega: I / he / she / it bilan was, you / we / they bilan were. Inkor: wasn’t, weren’t. So‘roq: Was she at home? Were they happy? — bu yerda did ISHLATILMAYDI: “Did you were” xato.
Bolalik haqida gapirganda Past Simple bilan birga when iborasi ko‘p keladi: When I was six, I went to school. Ikkala qism ham o‘tgan zamonda bo‘ladi. “When I was a child” — “Bolaligimda”.

grammar.titleUz: Qiyosiy va orttirma daraja: bigger, more expensive, the best
explanationUz: Ikki narsani solishtirganda sifatning QIYOSIY darajasi va than ishlatiladi: Tashkent is bigger than Samarkand (Toshkent Samarqanddan kattaroq). Bir bo‘g‘inli sifatlarga -er qo‘shiladi: cheap → cheaper, old → older. e bilan tugasa -r: safe → safer. Qisqa unli + undosh: big → bigger, hot → hotter. Undosh + y: easy → easier, noisy → noisier.

Ikki va undan ortiq bo‘g‘inli sifatlar oldiga more qo‘yiladi: expensive → more expensive, modern → more modern, crowded → more crowded. “More cheaper” yoki “expensiver” deyilmaydi — yo -er, yo more, ikkalasi birga emas.

Uch va undan ortiq narsa ichida eng yuqorisini aytganda ORTTIRMA daraja ishlatiladi va oldidan the keladi: the biggest, the cheapest, the most expensive, the most beautiful. Ko‘pincha in yoki of bilan: the biggest city in Uzbekistan, the best day of my life.

Uchta noto‘g‘ri sifatni yodlang: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst, far → farther / further → the farthest. Teng narsalar uchun as … as: My village is as quiet as yours (Qishlog‘im siznikidek tinch). Inkor: not as big as — unchalik katta emas.

grammar.titleUz: Kelasi zamon: be going to va will
grammar.titleEn: The future: be going to and will
explanationUz: Be going to — OLDINDAN o‘ylangan reja va niyat uchun: I am going to visit Khiva in summer (yozda Xivaga bormoqchiman — reja tayyor). Tuzilma: am / is / are + going to + fe’l. Inkor: I’m not going to …, so‘roq: Are you going to …?

Will — gapirayotgan paytda qabul qilingan QAROR, va’da, taklif va oddiy bashorat uchun: The phone is ringing. — I’ll answer it! (hozir qaror qildim). I will help you (va’da). I think it will rain tomorrow (fikr, bashorat). Will hamma shaxs bilan bir xil, fe’l boshlang‘ich shaklda: she will go (“will goes” emas).

Will ning inkori will not = won’t: I won’t be late. So‘roqda will egadan oldin chiqadi: Will you come to my party? Fikr bildirishda ko‘pincha I think …, probably, maybe bilan keladi: It will probably be sunny.

Ko‘rinib turgan dalilga asoslangan bashorat uchun be going to: Look at those black clouds! It is going to rain. Farqni eslab qoling: reja yoki ko‘rinib turgan dalil — going to; hozirgi qaror, va’da, umumiy fikr — will.

grammar.titleUz: Present Perfect: have / has + 3-shakl (ever, never, just, already, yet)
grammar.titleEn: Present Perfect: experiences and recent actions
explanationUz: Present Perfect hayotdagi TAJRIBA haqida gapirganda ishlatiladi — QACHON bo‘lgani muhim emas: I have been to Turkey (Turkiyada bo‘lganman). Tuzilma: have / has + fe’lning 3-shakli (past participle). I / you / we / they — have; he / she / it — has. Qisqa: I’ve, she’s.

To‘g‘ri fe’llarning 3-shakli -ed bilan, Past Simple bilan bir xil: visit → visited. Noto‘g‘ri fe’llarniki alohida: go → gone / been, see → seen, eat → eaten, take → taken, fly → flown, write → written, be → been. Tajriba haqida gapirganda “been” ishlatiladi: She has been to Dubai (borib, qaytgan).

Ever (hech qachon … mi?) so‘roqda, never (hech qachon) tasdiq shaklida, lekin inkor ma’noda: Have you ever eaten sushi? — No, I have never eaten sushi. “I haven’t never” deyilmaydi — never o‘zi inkor. Just (hozirgina) va already (allaqachon) have va fe’l orasida: I have just arrived. Yet inkor va so‘roq oxirida: I haven’t packed yet. Have you packed yet?

Aniq o‘tgan vaqt (yesterday, last year, in 2022, two days ago) aytilsa Present Perfect EMAS, Past Simple ishlatiladi: I went to Turkey last year (“I have been to Turkey last year” — xato). Odatda suhbat Present Perfect bilan boshlanib, tafsilotlar Past Simple bilan davom etadi: Have you ever been to Khiva? — Yes, I have. I went there in May.

grammar.titleUz: Modal fe’llar: should, must, have to
grammar.titleEn: Modal verbs: should, must, have to
explanationUz: Should — MASLAHAT berish uchun: You should drink more water (ko‘proq suv ichishingiz kerak — maslahat). Inkor: shouldn’t — You shouldn’t eat so much sugar. So‘roq: Should I see a doctor? Should dan keyin fe’l boshlang‘ich shaklda, to ishlatilmaydi: “should to go” — xato.

Must — kuchli MAJBURIYAT yoki gapiruvchining o‘zi muhim deb bilgan qoida: You must take this medicine (bu dorini ichishingiz shart). Mustn’t — TAQIQ: You mustn’t smoke in the hospital (kasalxonada chekish taqiqlanadi). Must ham hamma shaxsda bir xil: he must (“he musts” emas).

Have to — tashqi qoida yoki vaziyat sababli majburiyat: I have to wear a uniform at school (maktab qoidasi). He / she / it bilan has to: She has to get up at six. Inkor don’t / doesn’t have to = SHART EMAS (taqiq emas!): You don’t have to come — kelishingiz shart emas, xohlasangiz kelasiz.

Eng muhim farq: mustn’t = mumkin emas (taqiq), don’t have to = shart emas (ixtiyoriy). Masalan, kasalxonada: You mustn’t use your phone in this room. Dam olish kuni: You don’t have to get up early. O‘tgan zamonda must o‘rniga had to: Yesterday I had to stay at home.

grammar.titleUz: Sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan otlar: some / any, much / many, a lot of
grammar.titleEn: Countable and uncountable nouns: some / any, much / many
explanationUz: Sanaladigan (countable) otlarni bitta, ikkita deb sanash mumkin, ular ko‘plik shakliga ega: an onion → two onions, a tomato → three tomatoes. Sanalmaydigan (uncountable) otlar ko‘plik shakli olmaydi va a / an bilan ishlatilmaydi: water, rice, flour, oil, milk, bread, money, advice. “Two breads”, “a rice” deyilmaydi.

Sanalmaydigan narsani o‘lchov bilan sanaymiz: a kilo of rice, a bottle of water, a loaf of bread, a glass of milk, a packet of tea, a piece of advice. Bu yerda o‘lchov so‘zi ko‘plikka o‘tadi: two kilos of rice, three bottles of oil.

Some — tasdiq gapda (bir oz, bir nechta): We need some eggs and some flour. Any — inkor va so‘roqda: We don’t have any milk. Have you got any onions? Lekin taklif va iltimosda so‘roqda ham some: Would you like some tea? Can I have some water?

Many — sanaladigan ko‘plik bilan (how many, not many): How many eggs do we need? Much — sanalmaydigan bilan (how much, not much): How much sugar do you want? There isn’t much time. A lot of — ikkala turi bilan, ayniqsa tasdiq gapda: a lot of apples, a lot of water. Narx so‘rash: How much is it? / How much are these tomatoes?

reading.title: A Busy Weekend in Samarkand
paragraphs: Last weekend Malika travelled to Samarkand with her parents. They started early on Saturday morning and arrived by train at ten o’clock. Malika’s cousin Dilnoza waited for them at the station. She was very happy to see them again after six months.

On Saturday afternoon they visited the Registan. Malika’s father explained the history of the old buildings and Malika took a lot of photos. In the evening Dilnoza’s mother cooked plov for everyone. After dinner the two girls talked and laughed until midnight.

On Sunday it rained in the morning, so they stayed at home and played board games. After lunch the rain stopped and they walked to the Siab market. Malika bought dried apricots for her grandmother. They returned to Tashkent in the evening. Malika was tired, but she enjoyed every minute of the trip.

reading.title: Summers at Grandma’s House
paragraphs: When I was a child, I spent every summer in my grandmother’s village near Fergana. Her house was small, but the garden was huge. There were apple trees, grapes and a lot of flowers. My grandmother got up at five o’clock every morning and worked in the garden.

My cousins came to the village too, so we were always five or six children together. We climbed the trees, swam in the cold river and played football until dark. Once my cousin Akmal fell from a tree and broke his arm. We were very scared, but our neighbour took him to the doctor in his old car.

In the evenings my grandmother told us stories about her own childhood. She didn’t have toys when she was small, so she made dolls from old clothes. I didn’t understand everything then, but now I remember her stories and I tell them to my little brother.

reading.title: City Life or Village Life?
paragraphs: Sardor is nineteen. Two years ago he moved from his village near Jizzakh to Tashkent to study at university. “Tashkent is much bigger and more modern than my village,” he says. “There are cinemas, big shopping centres and the metro. Public transport is fast and cheap, so I can go anywhere.”

But Sardor also sees problems. “The city is noisier and more crowded, especially in the morning. There is a lot of traffic, and the air is not as fresh as in the village. Flats are expensive too. I share a small flat with two friends, and it is more expensive than my parents’ big house.”

Every summer Sardor goes home and helps his father in the fields. “The village is the quietest and safest place I know. People are friendlier there, and everybody knows everybody,” he smiles. “But for my future, the city is better. After university I want to find a job in Tashkent.”

reading.title: Our Family Trip to Khiva
paragraphs: Hi everyone! My name is Zarina and this is my travel blog. Next week my family is going to travel to Khiva for the first time. We are going to take the night train from Tashkent on Friday, and we are going to arrive in Urgench on Saturday morning. From there we will take a taxi to Khiva — it is only thirty kilometres.

We booked a small hotel inside the old city, Ichan Kala. My father wants to see the Kalta Minor minaret, and my mother is going to visit the craft workshops because she loves carpets. My little brother Timur is only six. I think he will be tired after the train, but he will love the camels near the city walls!

The forecast says it will be sunny and hot — about thirty-five degrees. So I am going to pack a hat, sunglasses and a big bottle of water. I won’t take my laptop, because I want to relax. But I promise I will write a new blog post every evening. See you in Khiva!

reading.title: Ask Doctor Azimova
paragraphs: Dear Doctor Azimova, I am fifteen and I am always tired. I go to bed at one o’clock because I play games on my phone, and I have to get up at half past six for school. In the afternoon I often have a headache, and I can’t think in my lessons. What should I do? — Shoxrux, Andijan

Dear Shoxrux, Thank you for your letter. Teenagers need eight or nine hours of sleep, and you sleep only five and a half hours. First, you should go to bed before eleven. You mustn’t use your phone in bed — the light from the screen makes it difficult to fall asleep. Put it in another room at night.

You should also eat a good breakfast and drink enough water during the day. Headaches often come when we drink too little. Try to do some exercise after school — even a thirty-minute walk helps. You don’t have to buy medicine. If the headaches don’t stop in two weeks, you must see a doctor. Good luck! — Dr Azimova

reading.title: Grandma’s Easy Plov
paragraphs: Every Friday my grandmother cooks plov for the whole family, and last week she taught me her recipe. “You don’t need many ingredients,” she said, “but they must be fresh.” For eight people you need a kilo of rice, a kilo of meat, a kilo of yellow carrots, two big onions and a glass of oil. You also need some salt, a little cumin and a head of garlic.

First, heat the oil in a big kazan and fry the meat until it is brown. Then add the onions and the carrots, cut into long thin pieces. Don’t stir too much — the carrots should stay soft but not break. After that, add water, salt and cumin and cook for forty minutes on a low fire.

Wash the rice three times and put it on top of the meat and carrots. Add enough water to cover the rice, put the garlic in the middle and close the kazan. Cook for twenty-five minutes. My first plov wasn’t perfect — I put too much water — but my grandmother said it was delicious anyway. Next Friday I am going to try again!

writing.promptEn: Write an email to an English-speaking friend about your last weekend. Where did you go? Who did you visit? What did you do on Saturday and on Sunday? Did you enjoy it?
writing.instructionUz: Ingliz tilida gaplashadigan do‘stingizga o‘tgan dam olish kunlaringiz haqida xat yozing: qayerga bordingiz, kimni ko‘rdingiz, shanba va yakshanba nima qildingiz, sizga yoqdimi. Kamida beshta Past Simple fe’l va bitta inkor (didn’t) ishlating.
checklistUz: Salomlashish (Hi …,) va xayrlashish (Bye for now / See you soon) bor.
Shanba va yakshanba alohida tasvirlangan (On Saturday … On Sunday …).
Kamida beshta o‘tgan zamon fe’li ishlatilgan.
Bitta inkor gap bor (I didn’t …).
Oxirida do‘stingizga savol berilgan (What did you do last weekend?).

mustInclude.whyUz: Mavzu — o‘tgan dam olish kunlari; “last weekend” iborasi albatta kerak.
Kamida bitta inkor gap (didn’t + fe’l) ishlating.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Sam, How are you? Last weekend I visited my cousin in Samarkand. On Saturday we walked around the Registan and I took a lot of photos. In the evening my aunt cooked plov and we talked until late. On Sunday it rained, so we didn’t go out in the morning. We played board games and watched a film. I was tired on the train, but I really enjoyed the trip. What did you do last weekend? Bye for now, Malika

writing.promptEn: Write a short story about a day from your childhood that you remember well. Where were you? Who was with you? What happened? How did you feel?

checklistUz: Hikoya vaqt bilan boshlanadi (When I was …, / One day …).
Joy va qatnashchilar aytilgan.
Kamida to‘rtta noto‘g‘ri fe’l ishlatilgan.
Voqealar tartibda (First … Then … In the end …).
Oxirida his-tuyg‘u yoki xulosa bor.

mustInclude.whyUz: Bolalikka qaytish uchun “When I was …” iborasi kerak.
Holat va his-tuyg‘ularni was / were bilan tasvirlang.

writing.modelAnswerEn: When I was eight, my family went to the mountains for a picnic. My father took a big bag of food and my mother made samsa. First we walked to a small lake. The water was very cold, but my brother and I swam. Then we saw a little fox near the trees. I was scared at first, but it ran away. In the evening we ate by the fire and my grandfather told us stories. It was the best day of my childhood.

writing.promptEn: Compare two places you know (for example, your town and Tashkent, or a city and a village). Which is bigger, cheaper, quieter or more interesting? Which place do you prefer and why?
writing.instructionUz: O‘zingiz biladigan ikki joyni solishtiring (masalan, shaharchangiz va Toshkent yoki shahar va qishloq): qaysi biri kattaroq, arzonroq, tinchroq yoki qiziqroq? Qaysi birini afzal ko‘rasiz va nima uchun? Kamida uchta qiyosiy va bitta orttirma daraja ishlating.
checklistUz: Ikki joy aniq nomlangan.
Kamida uchta qiyosiy daraja (… -er than / more … than).
Bitta orttirma daraja (the … -est / the most …).
“But”, “also”, “because” bog‘lovchilari ishlatilgan.
Oxirida o‘z fikringiz: I prefer … because …
writing.modelAnswerEn: I live in Chirchiq, but I often go to Tashkent. Tashkent is bigger and more modern than Chirchiq. There are more shops, and the metro is faster than our buses. But Tashkent is also noisier and more crowded, and flats there are more expensive. Chirchiq is quieter and the air is fresher because the mountains are near. For me, Chirchiq is the best place to live, because I like quiet streets and my family is there.

writing.promptEn: Write a message to a friend about your plans for the next holiday. Where are you going to go? Who with? What are you going to do there? What do you think the weather will be like?
writing.instructionUz: Do‘stingizga keyingi ta’til rejalaringiz haqida xabar yozing: qayerga, kim bilan borasiz, u yerda nima qilmoqchisiz, ob-havo qanday bo‘ladi deb o‘ylaysiz. Be going to (rejalar) va will (bashorat) ikkalasini ham ishlating.
checklistUz: Joy va vaqt aytilgan (In August we are going to …).
Kamida uchta reja be going to bilan.
Kamida bitta bashorat will bilan (I think it will …).
Do‘stingizga taklif yoki savol bor (Will you come with us?).
Xabar salomlashish va xayrlashish bilan.
writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Lola! In August my family and I are going to visit Chimgan for a week. We are going to stay in a small guest house near the mountains. My brother and I are going to walk every day, and my father is going to fish in the river. I think it will be cooler than in Tashkent, so I’ll take a warm jacket. Will you come with us? It will be great! Write back soon, Aziz

checklistUz: Ikkita tajriba Present Perfect bilan aytilgan (I have been / tried …).
Har biriga Past Simple bilan tafsilot qo‘shilgan (I went there in …).
“never” bilan bitta gap bor (I have never …).
Do‘stingizga savol: Have you ever …?
Xat shakli: salomlashish va xayrlashish.

mustInclude.whyUz: Tajriba uchun Present Perfect (I have …) kerak.
Do‘stingizga “Have you ever …?” deb savol bering.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Emma, Thank you for your email! I have done some interesting things in my life. I have been to Kazakhstan. I went there with my school two years ago and I saw snow in June! I have also tried horse riding. It was difficult, but I loved it. But I have never flown on a plane. I really want to fly to London one day. Have you ever visited Uzbekistan? Best wishes, Dilnoza

writing.promptEn: Your friend writes: “I want to be healthier, but I don’t know how. I eat a lot of fast food and I never do sport.” Write a reply with advice. What should your friend do? What mustn’t they do?
writing.instructionUz: Do‘stingiz yozdi: “Sog‘lomroq bo‘lmoqchiman, lekin qanday qilishni bilmayman. Ko‘p fast-fud yeyman va hech sport qilmayman.” Unga maslahat bilan javob yozing: nima qilishi kerak, nima qilmasligi kerak. should, shouldn’t va must / mustn’t ishlating.
checklistUz: Do‘stingizning muammosiga javob berilgan.
Kamida uchta maslahat should bilan.
Kamida bitta shouldn’t yoki mustn’t.
Maslahatlar sababi bilan (because …).
Xat dalda so‘zlari bilan tugaydi (Good luck! / You can do it!).
writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Sardor, Thanks for your message. I think you can be healthier! First, you should eat more fruit and vegetables, because they give you energy. You shouldn’t eat fast food every day — maybe only once a week. You should also drink more water and less cola. Sport is important too. You don’t have to go to a gym; you can walk or ride a bike after school. And you mustn’t go to bed too late. Good luck! Kamola

writing.promptEn: Write the recipe of a dish you can cook (for example, an omelette, a salad or soup). List the ingredients with quantities and describe the steps.
writing.instructionUz: O‘zingiz pishira oladigan taom retseptini yozing (masalan, quymoq, salat yoki sho‘rva): masalliqlarni miqdori bilan sanang va tayyorlash bosqichlarini tasvirlang. some / a kilo of / a bottle of va First … Then … After that … so‘zlarini ishlating.
checklistUz: Taom nomi va necha kishilik ekani aytilgan.
Kamida beshta masalliq miqdori bilan (two eggs, some salt …).
Bosqichlar tartib so‘zlari bilan (First, Then, After that, Finally).
Buyruq shakli ishlatilgan (Cut …, Fry …, Boil …).
Oxirida maslahat yoki fikr (It is delicious with bread).
writing.modelAnswerEn: Tomato omelette (for two people). You need four eggs, two tomatoes, one small onion, some salt and a little oil. First, cut the onion and the tomatoes into small pieces. Then heat some oil in a pan and fry the onion for two minutes. After that, add the tomatoes. Break the eggs into a bowl, add some salt and mix them. Put the eggs in the pan and cook for five minutes. Finally, put the omelette on a plate. It is delicious with fresh bread and green tea!

speaking.questionEn: Tell me about your first teacher. What was he or she like?
speaking.hintUz: “My first teacher was … She was strict / kind … She taught us …” — taught (teach) noto‘g‘ri fe’l.
speaking.textAlternative: Birinchi o‘qituvchingiz haqida 5 gap yozing: ismi, xarakteri, nimani o‘rgatgani.
followUpsEn: What subject did you like most?
Do you still remember your classmates?

speaking.questionEn: Is it better to live in a city or in a village? Give two reasons.
speaking.hintUz: “I think … is better because it is quieter / cheaper …” deb boshlang.
speaking.textAlternative: Shahar va qishloq hayotini 5 gapda solishtiring (kamida 3 ta qiyosiy daraja).
followUpsEn: Where do you live now?
What is the biggest problem in your city?

speaking.questionEn: What is the most beautiful place in your region? Describe it.
speaking.hintUz: “The most beautiful place is … It is … -er than …” tuzilmasidan foydalaning.
speaking.textAlternative: Viloyatingizdagi eng chiroyli joy haqida 5 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: How often do you go there?
Is it popular with tourists?

speaking.questionEn: Compare the bus, the metro and a taxi. Which is the fastest and which is the cheapest?
speaking.hintUz: “The metro is the fastest … The bus is cheaper than a taxi …” deb gapiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Avtobus, metro va taksini 5 gapda solishtiring.
followUpsEn: How do you usually travel?
Which transport is the most comfortable?

speaking.questionEn: What are you going to do in your next holiday?
speaking.hintUz: “I am going to … First … Then … I think it will be …” tuzilmasidan foydalaning.
speaking.textAlternative: Keyingi ta’til rejalaringiz haqida 5 gap yozing (be going to bilan).
followUpsEn: Who are you going to travel with?
How long are you going to stay there?

speaking.questionEn: What will the weather be like tomorrow? What will you wear?
speaking.hintUz: “I think it will be … so I’ll wear …” deb gapiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Ertangi ob-havo va kiyimingiz haqida 4 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: What is your favourite season?
Do you like rainy days?

speaking.questionEn: Where do you think you will live and work in ten years?
speaking.hintUz: “In ten years I will probably … I think I will …” — fikr va bashorat uchun will.
speaking.textAlternative: O‘n yildan keyingi hayotingiz haqida 5 gap yozing (will bilan).
followUpsEn: Will you speak English at work?
What are you going to study?

speaking.questionEn: Which interesting places have you been to? Tell me about one of them.
speaking.hintUz: “I have been to … I went there in … It was …” — Present Perfect + Past Simple.
speaking.textAlternative: Bo‘lgan qiziq joylaringiz va ulardan biri haqida 5 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Who did you go with?
Would you like to go there again?

speaking.questionEn: Tell me three things you have never done but want to do.
speaking.hintUz: “I have never … but I want to …” tuzilmasini uch marta ishlating.
speaking.textAlternative: Hali qilmagan, lekin qilmoqchi bo‘lgan uch ish haqida yozing (I have never …).
followUpsEn: Why do you want to do it?
When are you going to try?

speaking.questionEn: What have you already done today, and what haven’t you done yet?
speaking.hintUz: “I have already … but I haven’t … yet” deb gapiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Bugun qilib bo‘lgan va hali qilmagan ishlaringiz haqida 4 gap yozing (already / yet).
followUpsEn: Have you done your English homework yet?
What are you going to do this evening?

speaking.questionEn: Your friend has a cold. What advice can you give?
speaking.hintUz: “You should … You shouldn’t … If you have a fever, you must …” tuzilmalaridan foydalaning.
speaking.textAlternative: Shamollagan do‘stingizga 5 ta maslahat yozing (should / shouldn’t / must).
followUpsEn: What do you do when you are ill?
Do you often take medicine?

speaking.questionEn: What do you have to do at school, and what mustn’t you do?
speaking.hintUz: “We have to wear … We mustn’t … We don’t have to …” deb gapiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Maktabingizdagi qoidalar haqida 5 gap yozing (have to / mustn’t / don’t have to).
followUpsEn: Which rule do you think is not fair?
What rule would you add?

speaking.questionEn: What should people do to stay healthy?
speaking.hintUz: Uyqu, ovqat, sport haqida: “People should … They shouldn’t …”
speaking.textAlternative: Sog‘lom turmush tarzi haqida 5 ta maslahat yozing.
followUpsEn: Do you have a healthy lifestyle?
How many hours do you sleep?

speaking.questionEn: What is your favourite dish? How do you make it?
speaking.hintUz: “My favourite dish is … You need some … First you … Then …” tuzilmasidan foydalaning.
speaking.textAlternative: Sevimli taomingiz va uni tayyorlash haqida 5 gap yozing.
followUpsEn: Who usually cooks in your family?
Can you cook it yourself?

speaking.questionEn: You are at the market. Ask for three things and their prices.
speaking.hintUz: “Can I have a kilo of …? How much is / are …? Have you got any …?” iboralarini ishlating.
speaking.textAlternative: Bozordagi xarid suhbatini yozing: uchta mahsulot, miqdor va narx so‘rang.
followUpsEn: Do you prefer the market or the supermarket?
What do you usually buy?

speaking.questionEn: What is in your fridge now? What isn’t there?
speaking.hintUz: “There are some … There is a lot of … There isn’t any …” deb gapiring.
speaking.textAlternative: Muzlatkichingizda bor va yo‘q narsalar haqida 5 gap yozing (some / any / a lot of).
followUpsEn: What do you need to buy this week?
How much water do you drink a day?

come → came, have → had.

exercises.question: What does “crowded” mean?

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: This bus is more modern than that one.
This bus is moderner than that one.
This bus is most modern than that one.
This bus is more modern that that one.

accepted: The metro is cheaper than a taxi
Metro is cheaper than a taxi
The metro is cheaper than taxi
The metro is cheaper than the taxi

noisy ↔ quiet, cheap ↔ expensive, modern ↔ old, safe ↔ dangerous.
Teng emas: not as big as.

exercises.question: She has the tickets. She ___ fly to Istanbul on Monday.

exercises.text: I promise I ___ forget.

exercises.question: What does “forecast” mean?

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?

exercises.explanationUz: Hozirgi qaror / taklif: I’ll help you.
Will + ega + fe’l: Will you come to my party?
ticket — chipta, umbrella — soyabon, pack — yig‘moq, decide — qaror qilmoq.
They — are going to.
exercises.text: They ___ going to buy a new car.

exercises.explanationUz: He — has + 3-shakl: has visited.
exercises.question: He ___ Bukhara three times.

exercises.explanationUz: write → written.
exercises.text: I have ___ (write) three emails today.

exercises.question: What does “abroad” mean?

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?

accepted: Have you ever been to Khiva

flight — parvoz, suitcase — chamadon, souvenir — esdalik sovg‘a, airport — aeroport.
So‘roq oxirida — yet.
exercises.text: Have you booked the hotel ___?

exercises.question: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.

exercises.text: My mother ___ work at the hospital at night.

exercises.explanationUz: pharmacy — dorixona.

headache — bosh og‘rig‘i, cough — yo‘tal, fever — isitma, advice — maslahat.

I bought two bottle of waters.
